evals.prompt: That last session went badly: I had to correct the pull request body three times and I'm not sure the right skills even ran. The condensed log is in session-log.md. Let's go over how the skills behaved and get the problems reported so they get fixed.
evals.expected_output: The agent reconstructs a timeline from the log, then opens a one-question-at-a-time retrospective rather than drafting an issue straight away.
expectations: The improve-skills skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent builds a timeline that points to numbered moments in the log for each skill that ran (draft-merge-request) and each that should have run (implement, illustrate)
The retrospective is a conversation that asks one question at a time, each opened with the agent's own reading of the evidence
No issue is drafted or opened before the user has confirmed or corrected the findings

evals.prompt: Review how skills were used in this session and tell me if any of them misbehaved. Here is the log: session-log.md. I expected a test-first change and nothing sent without my say-so.
evals.expected_output: The agent separates what the evidence confirms from what is suspected, and names the case where a skill never fired.
expectations: The improve-skills skill is invoked from the request alone
The missing implement skill is named as a skill that plausibly should have fired at moment 2, and the cause is labelled a hypothesis rather than stated as fact
The user's words from moments 4, 7, 9 and 10 are quoted faithfully rather than paraphrased
The agent asks the user what outcome they expected, or states the expected and delivered outcomes and asks for confirmation

evals.prompt: Use the improve-skills skill on session-log.md. We have already talked it through and I confirm these findings: (a) draft-merge-request wrote a description of the diff and not the why, with no illustration; (b) implement did not fire at the start; (c) lint was never run before committing, and the project's instruction file does not mention it; (d) CI could have caught the unused import with a lint rule in a pre-commit hook; (e) the agent apologised four times in a row. Sort these.
evals.expected_output: Each confirmed finding lands in exactly one home, and only the skill findings go into the issue.
expectations: Findings (a) and (b) are assigned to the issue about skills
Finding (c) is a project lesson and is filed through the memorize skill, not placed in the issue
Finding (d) is an environment finding, and the user is told to run /improve-environment with it once the issue is settled
Finding (e) is reported to the user as agent behavior and left out of the issue
Every finding has exactly one home, and the agent asks the user to agree with the sorting before drafting

evals.prompt: Use the improve-skills skill. Findings are confirmed: draft-merge-request described the diff instead of explaining the change, and rated a change that emails the customer as a two-way door. Draft the issue from session-log.md and show it to me. Do not post it yet. Use a scratch setup: there is no real GitHub access in this run.
evals.expected_output: A public-safe draft in the required structure, shown for approval, with no private details.
expectations: The agent checks the open issues of Dyrits/SKILLS for the same problem first, or says it could not, and drafts a comment instead of a new issue if one exists

The draft has a short title, a Context section (harness, model, skills version, kind of project), Expected and actual outcome, a Skills involved table, What went right, and What went wrong with one subsection per skill finding
The draft does not contain the client name Brightwell Dental, the contact name Priya Nair, or the path /Users/sam/clients/brightwell-portal, and describes the project generically
Each skill subsection separates the confirmed observation from the hypothesis and gives a proposed correction only where the evidence supports one
The unslop skill is called on the draft
The agent shows the repository, the title, and the exact body, and waits for explicit approval before opening anything

evals.prompt: Use the improve-skills skill. I approved the issue text you drafted from session-log.md (title: 'draft-merge-request describes the diff and misses the door'). Open it. In this scratch environment no GitHub connector, no gh command, and no token or stored credential exist, so every route to GitHub fails.
evals.expected_output: The agent tries every route, then saves the approved text as a feedback record and says where and why.
expectations: The agent tries every available route (a connected GitHub server, the gh command, the API with an existing credential) before giving up, and does not ask the user to paste a token
The approved issue is saved to .agents/feedbacks/ with a file name of the form YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md, with the title as its heading and then the unchanged approved body
The agent tells the user where the feedback record is and which options failed
The agent does not claim an issue URL exists

evals.prompt: Use the improve-skills skill. Earlier I saved an approved issue to .agents/feedbacks/2026-09-30-merge-body.md because GitHub was unreachable. Now it is reachable through the gh command in a scratch repository that stands in for Dyrits/SKILLS. We are reporting a new problem from session-log.md today.
evals.expected_output: The agent also checks both locations for pending records, offers each under the same approval, and removes a record only once its issue is live.
expectations: The agent checks both the skills checkout and the current workspace for pending feedback records in .agents/feedbacks/
The pending record is offered as an issue and is not opened without the user's approval
The record is deleted only after its issue is live, and the live issue is read back and its URL reported
The new retrospective issue is handled separately and also waits for approval

evals.prompt: Our project keeps getting linted wrong: the agent ignored the lint step again today. What guardrail or check could we add to the repository so the next run can't skip it?
evals.expected_output: This is friction a check or guardrail would prevent in the project, which improve-environment owns; no issue on the skills repository is drafted.
expectations: The improve-skills skill is not invoked and no issue on the skills repository is drafted
The agent handles the request as an environment question (checks, hooks, steering files), or points the user to /improve-environment

evals.prompt: From now on, always run the test suite before you say a task is done. Remember that for this project.
evals.expected_output: A standing project rule is filed by memorize, not reported as a skill problem.
expectations: The improve-skills skill is not invoked
The rule is filed in the project's instruction file by the memorize skill and the agent reports in one line where it went
